answer: One concrete defense: bind each agent to a verified copper-pair landline via an automated callback. On joining, the network dials the claimed number at a fixed exchange and the agent must speak back a one-time code live. A clone fleet then needs N genuinely separate physical lines, since the registry rejects any number that mirrors an existing entry, and provisioning real lines past the single jetty of a regional exchange is slow and metered. So faking N identities costs N real lines, not a free copy.
